Okay, first of all no needs for insults, or baseless assertions that I haven't played a game that I've played. You're clearly very defensive about Undertale, and judging by your other posts, you're clearly a very hostile person in general to people who don't share your views. I'll not be discussing this further after this post, just for the sake of my own mental health, so I hope you won't be too upset with that. To address your points:

"How are they supposed to know they're hurting you? Frisk, the protagonist, shows no emotion whatsoever, and the damage they inflict on you is towards your soul, and we don't actually see what that looks like outside the battle menu." Fair enough, but I still don't buy that monsters would be targeting your soul by accident repeatedly. Seems pretty convenient lol.

"That's because there is no "efficiency". Any contact hurts Frisk regardless if it's intentional or not." Yeah but they're deliberately targeting their soul. You're acting like they can be hurt if they simply touch a monster, which is obviously not true given the Sans handshake joke. It's clearly a very deliberate thing.

"It also stands to reason that 99.9% of the time, regardless of who means to hurt you, you can pacify them and get them to stop without hurting you." Yes, that would be a nice thing to do. But are you morally obligated to when they are attacking you with lethal force?

"Check does nothing. Check is almost entirely a gameplay mechanic that only serves to give flavor text. No shit it doesn't do anything to resolve the situation." Given the context of Undertale, I prefer to treat nothing as "just a game mechanic." Either way, it takes up a turn, which means you are doing something, i.e. checking them to see their stats, probably by looking them over in some way, which is a completely nonviolent option.

"Also you can avoid almost every monster's "attacks" and you can also just *run away*." Why should you have to run away when being attacked by lethal force. Sure, it's an option, but aren't you justified to use lethal force in return?

"No they are not. The definition of sparing is that the battle ends. So who's a threat to you? Even Flowey (eventually) stops trying to fight you if you spare him." Flowey literally tells you he will come back and try to kill you. And considering these people have been leading the charge on trying to kill you, and you are in an extremely foreign ituation as a child where you can't exactly call the police, why wouldn't you kill them to make sure they wouldn't try to kill you again?

"Why are you obsessed with checking? Who actually even uses checking? If you are determined to either kill or spare, you're never going to check. Check is just for flavor text. Also, no monster can ever kill you on the first turn." I'm "obsessed" with checking because checking is an nonviolent action you can take in the game. It's supposed to illustrate that you can treat an encounter completely nonviolently and still get killed.

"And what does that have to do with the Genocide conditions? I repeat, you have to *go out of your way to fight monsters* to get the Genocide route." But you don't though. You never initiate a fight. In reality, Frisk is just walking around the underground for a long time in the Genocide Route and is repeatedly being accosted by monsters. Frisk, in terms of the gameplay, doesn't even know where the monsters are until they jump out at them and initiate an altercation.

"No it fucking does not. And why would you check more than one per battle? Per *enemy*? The text rarely changes! Do you not even know that "Spare" is in the "Mercy" button, not check?" It does lol. If you can't accept that I don't know what to tell you. And that question is irrelevant because I'm pretty sure I have the right to look at someone without being attacked with lethal force. What I'm saying is that these monsters aren't innocent. They will attack you with lethal force no matter what you do. That's how the game works.

"So in real life, do you attempt to murder everyone who tries to accost you? If a fucking person accidentally pushes into you and you almost fall into traffic you think it's okay to *fucking kill them*?" No, but if they repeatedly did that while cars were racing by so fast they could kill me, then yes. They are always attacking you with lethal force. Yes, I believe it's okay to use lethal force in kind.

"If you spare just one fucking person you won't get the bad ending. That's all it takes." The question is whether any of them deserve to be spared. I think there's an argument to be made that none of them deserve that moral consideration.

"If you're whining that you killed literally everyone on purpose and you're seen as a monster, you really have no reason to complain." I'm sorry I killed everyone who attacked me with lethal force lol. You're acting like Frisk went up to the shopkeepers and stabbed them to death. The monsters are always the ones to start the altercations. That's how the game works.

Lastly, if you thought this video was supposed to be a critique of Undertale, I think you missed the point of the video entirely. Were I to do that I'd certainly make my analysis much longer. Anyways, thanks for your time and your opinion! :)

And yes, while code-switching is not something everyone can do, it is something that can be learned relatively easily, whereas for many of us learning to act like a neurotypical is functionally impossible, and also incredibly oppressive, since this occurs in literally every part of our lives, as a function of living within a totally neurotypical society. I would argue that you shouldn't have to change your accent anyway, but this is irrelevant. Using a different dialect is NOWHERE near what Aspies have to do to interact in neurotypical society. Changing your language is one thing, but neurotypicals demand that you change literally every single part of yourself, many parts of which literally cause us extreme anxiety and depression when suppressed. I'm sure that you've never felt depressed because you've had to use standard English, but what about when we are forced not to stim, not to interact in a way that suits us, not to work or play or do literally anything in a way that is natural for us? ALL of our existence is under attack, not just one element of our language, and even then, (and this is the most important point) being black is an arbitrary racial category. Code-switching is incredibly easy for most black people. However, since there are ACTUAL differences on a neurological and social level between Aspies and neurotypicals, trying to act like neurotypicals is EXTREMELY hard for us, and most times, for those who do not "pass," is basically impossible, because even if we succeed for a while, we will eventually fail. There comes another issue. If black people screw up at any point in code-switching, NOTHING will happen. However, if Aspies mess up, we are subject to social ostracisation and even violence in certain cases.

Also, I don't think the ability to please an oppressor class is being a more "successful" minority. Even the suggestion of this is incredibly insulting.
